description: We are The Others, a fun, curious, and creative team of students from a Science and Art Center in Türkiye, guided by our advisor, Dr. Hamiyet Tuncel, a science teacher and STEM education researcher. Our team members are part of a physics project group and share a strong interest in space, astronomy, science, technology, and creative storytelling.
summary: Our project aims to make education fun for young kids. The project uses “Unity Game Engine” to bring the forgotten spacecrafts to life and tell their stories themselves. We hope this makes all this precious information more reachable and simpler for kids, so it can spread around the world. Various artificial intelliegence models has also aided us greatly, including famous models like “Claude” and “Gemini” etc… We tried to make the game as intruguing towards kids as possible, and we hope you enjoy it the way we did, thank you.
details:
What it does: Forsaken is a Unity game in which the player explores Mars and deep space as a robot looking for humanity. The player moves with W, A, S, D, follows on-screen arrows, and presses E to interact with stationary robots. Each robot shares its story, and the player collects a part.

Story: In 2178, humanity moves from Earth to Mars. After 150 years, harsh conditions force them to leave, and they forget Forsaken. The robot wakes up 80 years later, meets other abandoned machines on Mars and in space, and with their help reaches humanity and shows them the value of what they left behind.

How it uses real science: Each robot is a real NASA mission: for example, Viking 1 was planned for 90 days but worked for years, Sojourner was designed for about a week but operated for 83 sols, and Ingenuity was designed for five flights but made 72. The parts link to real technologies: Viking’s nuclear power, Spirit’s wheel system, Sojourner’s airbag landing, Ingenuity’s rotor, Pioneer’s antenna, and Dawn’s ion propulsion.

Impact: The game introduces children to historic missions in a fun and emotional way and encourages them to see engineering and science as connected.

Tools.:Unity (game development), Claude and Gemini (story, planning, and text support), Kling AI (AI-generated video footage), CapCut (video editing).

Creativity: The story is told from the point of view of the machines themselves, so players feel they are rescuing forgotten explorers rather than reading a history lesson.

Design factors: We considered age appropriateness (8–14), simple controls, short educational dialogues, and accuracy of all dates and numbers, which were checked against NASA sources.
dataRefs: Sojourner Rover – The first rover on Mars (1997)
Viking 1 & 2 Landers – First U.S. landers to operate on Mars (1976)
Phoenix & InSight Landers – Water ice digging and marsquake detection
Dawn Spacecraft – Mapped Vesta and Ceres
Ingenuity Helicopter – First aircraft on another planet
